note: States with a public, state-set rule for surcharging an at-fault car accident. Other states leave the size of the increase to each insurer's filed rating plan. New York's $2,000 rule (Ins. Law 2335) is left out until its July 1, 2026 sunset is confirmed extended. Re-check yearly.

CA.text: California insurers can count an accident against your driving record only if you were at least 51% to blame and it caused an injury, or more than $1,000 of total damage. A property-damage-only accident of $1,000 or less can't raise your rate as an at-fault accident.
CA.cite: 10 Cal. Code Regs. § 2632.13(b); Cal. Ins. Code § 1861.025

MA.text: Under the Massachusetts Safe Driver Insurance Plan, an at-fault accident is surchargeable only if the insurer pays more than $1,000 above your deductible on a collision or property damage claim (or more than $1,000 on an injury-only claim). Insurers may use their own approved plan instead, so check which one yours uses.

NC.text: North Carolina's Safe Driver Incentive Plan sets the increase by insurance points for 3 policy years: an at-fault accident with total property damage (including your own car) of $2,300 or less is 1 point (+40%), over $2,300 but under $3,850 is 2 points (+55%), and $3,850 or more, or injury costs over $1,800, is 3 points (+70%). A first $2,300-or-less property-damage-only accident gets no points if nobody licensed in your household has convictions or at-fault accidents in the last 3 years and there was no moving-violation conviction.
NC.cite: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 58-36-65; NC Department of Insurance, Safe Driver Incentive Plan
